formula_basis: ES_alpha = sigma * phi(z_{1-alpha}) / (1-alpha) for P&L ~ N(mu,sigma^2); VaR_alpha = mu + sigma * z_{1-alpha} where Phi(z_{1-alpha}) = 1-alpha; MAR33 anchor: parametric normal ES is the theoretical benchmark for the 97.5% ES standard.
weakest_point: Implementation defect: conflating ES multiplier (2.3376) with VaR multiplier (1.9600) understates tail-risk capital by 16.2% (ratio VaR/ES = 0.8385).

formula_basis: ES_alpha = sigma * phi(z_{1-alpha}) / (1-alpha) for P&L ~ N(mu,sigma^2); VaR_alpha = mu + sigma * z_{1-alpha} where Phi(z_{1-alpha}) = 1-alpha; MAR33 anchor: the 99% ES is used for stress testing and model validation comparisons.
weakest_point: Implementation defect: conflating ES multiplier (2.6650) with VaR multiplier (2.3263) understates tail-risk capital by 12.7% (ratio VaR/ES = 0.8729).

formula_basis: ES_LH = ES_10d * sqrt(LH / 10); MAR33 section 33.3: ES scaled by square root of liquidity horizon over 10-day base horizon for modellable risk factors.
weakest_point: The sqrt(LH/10) rule assumes i.i.d. returns with constant volatility; autocorrelation or volatility clustering in credit spreads invalidates the scaling.

computation.step_5_fractional_treatment_convention: Acerbi-Tasche fractional order statistic: ES = [sum_{i=1}^{floor(k)} L_(i) + (k - floor(k)) * L_(ceil(k))] / k

formula_basis: ES_alpha = (1/k) * [sum_{i=1}^{floor(k)} L_(i) + (k - floor(k)) * L_(ceil(k))] where k = n(1-alpha) and L_(i) are ascending-sorted P&L; MAR33 section 33.2: ES is the average of P&L in the tail beyond the VaR quantile.
weakest_point: With n=20 and alpha=97.5%, the tail contains k=0.5 observations, so ES equals the single worst observation (-8.5) under standard interpolation conventions; the estimate has zero statistical robustness and is entirely sample-dependent.
